item.title: Bengals activate LB Swayze Bozeman, G Brian Parker from injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals announced a pair of roster moves on Monday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals announced a pair of roster moves on Monday afternoon.

Linebacker Swayze Bozeman and guard Brian Parker have both been activated from injured reserve. They will both be available to play against the Commanders in Monday night's game in Washington.

Bozeman was claimed off of waivers during the offseason and he appeared in four games before going on injured reserve with a forearm injury. He had four tackles while playing a regular role on special teams in those contests.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and he was placed on injured reserve at the end of August. Parker has been dealing with a knee injury.

item.title: DK Metcalf will not be suspended for actions during Steelers-Eagles
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: According to multiple reports, while Metcalf has avoided a suspension, he may still be fined.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers receiver DK Metcalf will not be suspended for his actions during Sunday's loss to the Eagles, according to multiple Monday reports.

Metcalf, however, may still be fined.

Metcalf was ejected for committing two unsportsmanlike conduct fouls over the course of the game.

Metcalf then left the locker room without speaking to reporters. But spoke to them on Monday, denying the accusation that he was trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

It’s been a trying year for Metcalf, who has just 36 catches for 434 yards with two touchdowns in 10 games. That the receiver will not be suspended is a positive development for him. But Pittsburgh would surely like to see Metcalf increase his production and reduce the on-field antics that do not help the team.

item.title: Commanders activate Jacory Croskey-Merritt
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Commanders have made an addition to their offensive backfield ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders have made an addition to their offensive backfield ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was activated from injured reserve on Monday afternoon. The Commanders released cornerback Isaac Yiadom in a corresponding move.

Croskey-Merritt was a full participant in practice this week and he was listed as questionable on Washington's final injury report. He has missed the last four games with a groin injury.

Croskey-Merritt had 67 carries for 239 yards and two touchdowns in five games before his injury.

The Commanders listed Rachaad White as questionable with a heel injury that kept him out of practice Saturday. Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry are the other backs on the active roster for Washington.

item.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.

Head coach John Harbaugh said at his Monday press conference that Newsome suffered a high-ankle sprain. Harbaugh said that Newsome will be out multiple weeks as a result of the injury.

Newsome only played four snaps before being forced out of Sunday's game. He has 35 tackles, an interception and eight passes defensed in his nine appearances this season.

That play earned Newsome a three-year extension beyond the one-year deal he signed with the team in the offseason, but the Giants will have to turn elsewhere in the secondary for the near future.

item.title: Vikings "don't necessarily expect" Jordan Addison back this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.

Addison has missed the last two games with a thumb injury that required surgery, but O'Connell said last week that the outlook was "really encouraging" for Addison's return. The Vikings opted not to put him on injured reserve, which points to a return before missing four games but O'Connell didn't make it sound like that would happen against the Falcons this week.

"Encouraged about where Jordan's at," O'Connell said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. "Don't necessarily expect to have him this week but he's progressing really well for having just gotten that thing fixed."

The Vikings will host the Panthers in Week 13 and O'Connell's next update on Addison's progress may not come until closer to that matchup.

item.title: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator.
item.content:encoded:
Arizona is making a significant change to its coaching staff.

The Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Rallis, 33, was retained under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur after previously serving in the same role under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Rallis came with Gannon from Philadelphia, where Gannon had served as defensive coordinator and Rallis was linebackers coach.

The Cardinals have struggled mightily on defense this season, with the unit currently ranked No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 31 in points allowed. The team had offered little resistance in losses to the Rams and Chiefs in consecutive weeks, with both teams scoring 34 points.

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator. He was Pittsburgh’s DC under Mike Tomlin from 2022 to 2025. He previously served as defensive coordinator for the Lions and Bengals.

item.title: Super Bowl LXI will be shown in IMAX theaters
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Super Bowl will be shown on some very big screens this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Super Bowl will be shown on some very big screens this season.

ESPN's broadcast of Super Bowl LXI will be shown live in IMAX theaters as part of an agreement among the NFL, Disney and IMAX.

The game will air live in IMAX theaters in the U.S., Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. The show will include the game itself, the halftime show, pregame and postgame.

IMAX has grown increasingly popular for its huge, curved screens and immersive sound. The format is known for movies like The Odyssey, not for live sports, but the opportunity to watch the Super Bowl on the biggest screen in town will draw plenty of fans who will be curious to see what the game looks like on a screen so big that the players are larger than life.

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.

Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

Ferguson was on track to return earlier this month before suffering a hamstring injury at practice.

But now his ankle has not responded to treatment the way he or the team anticipated.

“Didn’t necessarily feel great, but he had a really good week of practice but you could still see he was kind of getting comfortable,” McVay said of the process with Ferguson, via Adam Grosbard of the Southern California News Group. “Took some meds to be able to do that. Gets the hamstring on a Friday, and then, as he's really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it, and it was like something in his deltoid and his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want.

“I don't know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it's just not coming along, and he wouldn't be able to be himself and put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete, some of the change of direction, moving him across the formation.”

Ferguson is now set to remain on injured reserve for the rest of the year.

A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Ferguson was able to appear in just three games this year, catching seven passes for 63 yards with a touchdown. He caught 11 passes for 231 yards with three TDs in 14 games as a rookie last year.

item.title: Shane Steichen says Colts have not shut down Alec Pierce for the season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.
item.content:encoded:
A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.

Pierce has not played since aggravating a heel injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2 and the Colts' recent roster moves have made it clear that they have shifted their attention to the 2027 season. While that may be the case, head coach Shane Steichen said on Monday that the team has not made any call about whether Pierce will return in their final six games.

"I know there's reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season," Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. "We have not made that determination. He's still going through his rehab process. The only way we'll put him out there is if he's 100 percent. We gotta be really smart."

Pierce has a short window to get to 100 percent before the season is over and bringing him back from a long layoff may not be the best way to ensure that he's at full strength for next season, so it may just be a matter of when rather than if the Colts ultimately decide to shut the wideout down until next year.

item.title: Terrion Arnold's lawyer seeks sanctions for discovery violation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida. And the case against him is moving forward.

On Monday, attorney Harvey Steinberg filed a motion for sanctions, arising from the alleged failure of the prosecution to timely disclose as discovery material.

The gist of the 13-page filing is that the prosecution withheld a statement from defendant Boakai Hilton until after another defendant, Arianna Del Valle, sat for a sworn, pre-trial deposition.

Hilton's statement, per the filing, conflicts with statements made by Del Valle. By not having the Hilton statement, Steinberg was unable to properly question Del Valle about the discrepancies.

On the surface, it's an easy fix. Steinberg should get another chance to question Del Valle under oath. At a deeper level, the situation (if it unfolded the way Steinberg alleges) speaks to the integrity of the process.

Prosecutors have immense power and discretion, which should be exercised at all times with the goal of doing justice. Sometimes, a blind desire to "win" can overcome the mandate to do justice, thereby corrupting the system.

Steinberg potentially has caught the prosecution with a hand in the cookie jar. Once the presiding judge realizes what happened, it could cause the judge to take a more dim view of the case against Arnold. It also could spread beyond this specific case, prompting skepticism regarding other prosecutions.

The Hillsborough County prosecutor's office is already dealing with an unrealted case in which "winning" may have trumped justice. A prosecutor recently resigned for failing to disclose during jury selection that the sister of a fellow prosecutor was in the jury pool for a rape trial. The woman ultimately served as the foreperson of the jury, which returned a conviction.

A new trial has been ordered, and the prosecutor who failed to disclose the relationship has resigned.

It all comes back to integrity. Are the prosecutors playing games in order get a conviction or a favorable plea deal, or are the prosecutors committed to justice in whatever form it may take?

If Steinberg's contentions are accurate, it looks like someone may have been trying to sandbag Arnold's defense in an effort to make it harder to draw helpful testimony out of a key witness. In a case like this, the cards should always be on the table — with no one trying to keep anything up their sleeve.

item.title: Report: Giants DC Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview for Maryland head coaching job
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.
item.content:encoded:
Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Wilson recently had a virtual interview with the University of Maryland. Maryland fired Mike Locksley last month after a 2-5 start to the season.

Wilson grew up in Maryland and played defensive back for the Terrapins. He was a graduate assistant at the school in 2007 and 2008 before embarking on an NFL career that has also included stints with the Rams, Jets, Eagles, Ravens and Titans.

Wilson is in his first year with the Giants. They rank 12th in points allowed and seventh in yards allowed this season.

item.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker is not in concussion protocol
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.

Canales said at his press conference that Coker is not in concussion protocol as the Panthers move toward their Week 12 game against the Buccaneers.

Coker went for a check after taking a hit from Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith during the 35-33 Panthers win. He had four catches for 47 yards during the game.

Coker has 35 catches for 440 yards and three touchdowns on the season. He is second on the team in receptions behind fellow wideout Tetairoa McMillan.

item.title: 49ers release WR Brandon Aiyuk
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Aiyuk will next go to waivers.
item.content:encoded:
They waited as long as they could to do what they knew all along they'd be doing.

Two weeks after 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers have released him.

The 49ers had received a two-week roster exemption upon Aiyuk's reinstatement. Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owed him no pay for the duration of the roster exemption.

He'll now go to waivers, and he undoubtedly will be unclaimed. After that, he'll become a free agent.

Many expect Aiyuk to sign with the Commanders, possibly with a practice-squad stint the first step back to the field.

Where he goes after that remains to be seen. Multiple contenders could use help at the position, if Aiyuk can perform like he did before the 2024 ACL tear that ultimately derailed his career.

item.title: Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza: With two starts against two elite defenses, I've seen improvement
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While Fernando Mendoza is still looking for his first win as a starting quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft displayed his considerable potential in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
While Fernando Mendoza is still looking for his first win as a starting quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft displayed his considerable potential in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.

Las Vegas was able to come back from down 17-0 to tie the game midway through the third quarter. Mendoza then engineered another touchdown drive midway through the fourth period to pull the Raiders within seven.

But the comeback effort ended when Mendoza threw a pick-six to Ja'Quan McMillian with just under two minutes left in regulation.

Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters on Monday that he saw Mendoza take steps in multiple areas.

“No. 1 is just the environment,” Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. “That's a very hostile environment, and I thought, overall, he did a good job of getting everybody on the same page. I thought he used his legs extremely well, extended some plays.

“For his second start in the NFL against two elite defenses, I've seen improvement.”

Kubiak also complimented Mendoza for the way he was able to bring the team back from being down 17.

“That's who he is. That's what he's made of,” Kubiak said. “I think back to us being backed up, him taking a sack and then him making a really big third-down throw to Jack Bech. That's what you need from your quarterback.”

Mendoza finished Sunday’s game 18-of-37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Mendoza’s next game will be his primetime debut, as the Raiders will face the Browns on Sunday night in Week 12.

item.title: 49ers extend G.M. John Lynch's contract
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the offseason, the 49ers quietly extended the contract of coach Kyle Shanahan.
item.content:encoded:
In the offseason, the 49ers quietly extended the contract of coach Kyle Shanahan. His partner has now gotten a new deal, too.

Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reports that the 49ers and G.M. John Lynch have agreed to a contract extension. Lynch, who also serves as the team's president of football operations, was hired in early 2017. The Hall of Fame safety previously had worked for Fox.

Glazer explains that Lynch's deal was due to expire after the 2026 season. Last night, Lynch and owner Jed York struck a handshake deal on a new contract before the Week 11 win over the Vikings.

With Shanahan and Lynch working together, the 49ers have qualified for a pair of Super Bowls. They have contended far more often than not, qualifying for the postseason in 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2025.

Before Shanahan and Lynch arrived, the 49ers hadn't been to the playoffs since 2013.

This year, the 9-1 49ers have the inside track to the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs. They arguably have an excellent chance to win the franchise's first Super Bowl since 1994.

item.title: Quinnen Williams: We executed better on defense, but we still gave up 30 points
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys defense was under the microscope all week due to the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and hand them to assistant Mike Pettine, but defensive tackle Quinnen Williams pointed to something else playing a leading role in the unit's performance on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys defense was under the microscope all week due to the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and hand them to assistant Mike Pettine, but defensive tackle Quinnen Williams pointed to something else playing a leading role in the unit's performance on Sunday.

Dallas did not allow a touchdown in the first half while building a 27-9 lead over the Titans and ended the day as 51-30 winners. Williams, who had two sacks and a forced fumble in the win, "no matter who called the call, no matter what call, the players on the field had to execute" and that he was "super proud" of the way that the group responded on Sunday.

Williams's pride in the performance did not obscure the fact that it was far from perfect.

"We still gave up 30 points," Williams said, via the team's website. "So we definitely got to go watch the film and learn from it and get better, because we know the defense we can be and we have a long way to go, and we have to take steps forward to get there."

The Titans are a one-win team, which makes them exactly the kind of opponent you want to see when trying to right the ship. The Cowboys have another losing team on deck with the Eagles coming to town on Thanksgiving and they'll have to keep pushing to improve to make Sunday's win a sign of things to come rather than a momentary blip for an underwhelming unit.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers calls DK Metcalf's ejection "disappointing," won't comment on message to him
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On certain subjects, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't stop talking.
item.content:encoded:
On certain subjects, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't stop talking. On other topics, he won't say a single word.

Regarding Sunday's ejection of Steelers receiver DK Metcalf from the 19-16 loss to the Eagles, Rodgers said far close to nothing than something.

"That was disappointing," Rodgers told reporters. "Obviously, we love DK. And I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening. But, yeah, we can't have two of those."

So what is Rodgers's message to Metcalf?

"I'm not going to tell you that," Rodgers said. "I'm going to talk to DK. We're real good friends, so."

The "I'm not going to tell you that" was unnecessary, but on brand. Rodgers flashes that aspect of his personality from time to time. And it surely will make those who have to ask him questions on a regular basis not miss him after he retires following the current season.

Besides, why is it such a secret? Rodgers already said it was "disappointing" and that "we can't have" that. He could have just said that's the message.

Really, what else would the message be? Metcalf needs to control his emotions. Given that Rodgers has been willing to call out others when it's required, why should Metcalf be exempt?

Maybe that's exactly what Metcalf needs in order to keep him from doing it again.

item.title: Steelers' offense is awful in loss to Eagles
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A Philadelphia defense that previously looked like it was packing it in on the season stepped up in a big way today.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers entered today's game looking like playoff contenders. The Eagles entered today's game looking like they had given up on the season. You'd have to be an idiot to think the Eagles could win today.

But as Chris Berman used to say to the late, great Tom Jackson on NFL Primetime, That's why they play the games.

It was the Eagles who came out looking like a team in contention, and the Steelers who came out flat in a 19-16 Eagles win in Philadelphia.

The Steelers' offense was awful, particularly running the ball. Aaron Rodgers was the leading rusher with 29 yards on five carries. Jaylen Warren, who has played so well for most of this season, managed just 28 yards on nine carries, and Rico Dowdle had 15 yards on five carries.

Pittsburgh didn't score a touchdown until 1:21 remained in the fourth quarter, Aaron Rodgers hit Max Hurleman in the end zone for 20 yards.

Steelers receiver DK Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls, the second of which was called as taunting but appeared to involve Metcalf trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. Metcalf finished the game with one catch for two yards and had the worst of his many bad games this season.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made four field goals, including a 53-yarder in the third quarter and a 55-yarder in the fourth quarter that kept Philly on top even as its offense stagnated.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton wasn't great, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards, but he showed a little bit of promise with both his arm and his legs, and played well enough that there's no reason the Eagles shouldn't stick with him and see what he can do. Saquon Barkley also wasn't great, but he did manage a 38-yard touchdown run.

The Steelers, who still haven't won in Philadelphia since 1965, fall to 6-4 on the season. The Eagles improve to 3-7.

item.title: DK Metcalf: I didn't try to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game after an altercation with the Eagles defensive back.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf left the stadium without talking to reporters about his ejection from Sunday's game against the Eagles, but he fielded questions from them about his altercation with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean at the team's facility on Monday.

Metcalf said he "was avoiding you all" when asked why he left before players were back in the locker room after the loss and was asked what DeJean did to elicit what DeJean described as an attempt to poke him in the eye. Metcalf initially said he couldn't remember what happened, but later denied that an eye poke was his intent.

"I didn’t try to poke him in the eye. I was just telling him. . . . I was just telling him to stop pushing me," Metcalf said, via Joe Rutter of the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review.

The personal foul that led to Metcalf's ejection was his second of the game and it could lead to a suspension. Metcalf called that and the notion of internal repercussions questions for others. Metcalf's 2025 suspension for an altercation with a fan in Detroit could factor into a suspension decision and Metcalf was asked why he has struggled to remain composed at times during games.

“You have to ask the people that seemingly do that to me,” Metcalf said.

If Metcalf keeps reacting the way he did in Detroit and on Sunday, people will likely continue to try to draw a reaction that will keep him from making plays to help the Steelers so he might want to figure out a different coping mechanism whenever he is back in the lineup.

item.title: Mike Vrabel on Drake Maye: We want to give him every opportunity to return at some point
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period after suffering a fractured fibula in the Week 10 loss to the Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period after suffering a fractured fibula in the Week 10 loss to the Lions.

But there’s still a possibility the quarterback could return to action in 2026.

With the wave of injuries the Patriots have dealt with this year, the club has not placed Maye on injured reserve — largely because the team can only have eight players return from the list.

Head coach Mike Vrabel detailed Maye’s situation during his Monday press conference as New England returns from its Week 11 bye.

“Right now, he’s not on the reserve list,” Vrabel said, via Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. “He’s not on injured reserve. He’s on the active roster. So that’s where it is today.

“I think that those things are obviously fluid, but want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don’t know when that will be. I’m not sure, but I also try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week.”

While the Patriots currently have just two available quarterbacks, Vrabel said on Monday that he doesn’t anticipate the team being interested in adding Daniel Jones — or any other QB.

In 10 games this season, Maye has completed 65.6 percent of his passes for 2,330 yards with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

item.title: Mike Vrabel says Pats don't plan to add another QB: Tommy DeVito is our starter
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period — if not the rest of the season — the Patriots are not currently inclined to add quarterback Daniel Jones.
item.content:encoded:
While Drake Maye is going to be out for an extended period — if not the rest of the season — the Patriots are not currently inclined to add quarterback Daniel Jones.

That's at least what head coach Mike Vrabel said in his Monday press conference as New England returns from its Week 11 bye.

"Tommy’s our starter. Tommy’s our starter,” Vrabel said, via Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, when asked directly about the possibility of adding Jones. “We’re excited about that. [He had a] good preseason. And Tommy’s improved. I know that going into the last game, I think that being thrown in there had some good plays, had some things that he can improve on and little things. I think that was probably the biggest thing, just saying, ‘Hey, getting back into game action, how do you work in the pocket?’ These are things that he got so much better on when he got here.

“So, starting with those things and managing the offense and being able to get us in and out of the huddle and the right plays and just get into a flow and a tempo. And I think that some of the things that we saw in training camp, a lot of those guys that he’ll be out there throwing to some of those guys that he worked with in training camp. So, I think that there’s some carryover there.”

The Patriots currently have two quarterbacks available in DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. But at least for now, New England isn’t planning to add a third quarterback to ease the practice load.

“I think that this is also a great opportunity for Behren to improve in those reps that him and Tommy may have been splitting or Tommy taking the majority of those,” Vrabel said. “I think that that’s a great opportunity for Behren to improve in that regard of running the show team and doing those things.

“So, we will look at everything. But again, I don’t think that that’s something that’s going to happen here in the next few days.”

DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Nov. 15 loss to the Lions.

The Patriots will be on the road to face the Chargers on Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
The Falcons announced a change to their roster coming out of their bye week.

They have waived linebacker Christian Harris. Safety Jammie Robinson was signed to the active roster off of the practice squad in a corresponding move.

Harris signed with the Falcons this offseason and appeared in seven games for Atlanta this season. Almost all of his playing time came on special teams and he was credited with four tackles.

Robinson has played in four games this season and has six tackles. He played in six games for the Falcons last season and 21 games for the Panthers over his first two seasons.

The Falcons also announced that they have signed cornerback Terell Smith to their practice squad.

item.title: Travis Kelce moves past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in TD catches by a tight end
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone.

And Kelce has also secured another milestone in his storied career.

Kelce capped the Chiefs’ first drive with an 8-yard touchdown catch, giving Kansas City an early 7-0 lead over Arizona.

The score also moved Kelce past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in touchdowns by a tight end. Only Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez are ahead of Kelce on the list.

The possession lasted 11 plays and went 72 yards to the end zone, taking 5:14 off the clock.

Patrick Mahomes was 4-of-5 on the drive for 36 yards, converting a pair of third downs. He hit Rashee Rice for a 15-yard gain on one third down and the touchdown to Kelce was the second.

Rookie Emmett Johnson is once again off to a strong start, taking six carries for 36 yards while also catching a screen for an 8-yard gain.

item.title: Cooper DeJean: DK Metcalf "just missed" poking me in the eye
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close.

“Just missed,” DeJean said, via the Philadelphia Inquirer.

Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game after multiple incidents and two personal foul penalties, but DeJean said nothing that happened during the game could explain what had Metcalf so upset.

“We were just competing,” DeJean said. “Things like that happen in football. It wasn’t anything crazy, and no one was really saying anything. It was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me, things like that, and then it obviously carried over to whatever that was when he got thrown out.”

Metcalf had just one catch for two yards before he was kicked out, and DeJean suspects that Metcalf is mostly upset with his own production.

“He wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game," DeJean said. "Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me.”

item.title: Malik Nabers on sideline moment: I was just trying to watch the game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers.
item.content:encoded:
Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers. Nabers eventually worked his way past Winston and moved toward the edge of the field.

So what was happening?

"I vaguely remember it," Nabers told reporters, via Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic. "But, I mean, I just remember me saying, 'I'm good. I'm good. I wanna get back to watching the defense play.' And that was really all, I think. Everything was going on, I was just telling the offense, 'Let's go, let's go,' I think. Jameis kind of [was] trying to calm me down, but I was fine. So I was just telling him, 'I'm good. I'm good. I just wanna watch the game."

The fact that Nabers navigated past Winston and got into position to watch the game seems to confirm Nabers's explanation. He just wanted to watch the game.

The problem is that Winston's reaction to Nabers's initial movement created the impression that something else was happening. No quotes on the situation have emerged from Winston. It would be interesting to know why he thought Nabers needed to be restrained at a time when restraint ultimately wasn't necessary.

Either way, the moment went viral — and more people will see that video and draw possibly inaccurate conclusions than will hear Nabers's explanation.

item.title: Officials deny Jaguars TD on sensational catch by Parker Washington
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Washington appeared to make a superb touchdown catch, but the officials and the replay office ruled it incomplete.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington made a leaping grab in the back of the end zone, got his feet down in bounds, and controlled the ball as he fell to the ground in the fourth quarter today against the Giants.

Or so it appeared.

The officials ruled it incomplete, and after the Jaguars challenged, the replay review ruled that Washington did not make the catch. The ruling of incomplete pass stood, and the Jaguars settled for a field goal that cut the Giants' lead to 20-9.

It was a highly questionable call, questioned even by former NFL referee Gene Steratore, the CBS rules analyst who said on the game broadcast that he thought it was a catch.

Washington is having a sensational season, and that was perhaps his greatest play yet — or at least it would have been, if it had been ruled a catch.

The Giants previously got a touchdown on a Jameis Winston quarterback sneak, even though replays appeared to show Winston's helmet hit the ground before the ball crossed the goal line. Now there have been two controversial touchdown calls, both in the Giants' favor.

item.title: Mike Evans TD and Parker Washington non-TD raise more questions about NFL catch rules
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Two big plays on Sunday renewed questions about what is and is not a catch in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Few topics in the NFL cause more heated debates than what is or is not a catch. Two more big debates happened on Sunday, with two touchdown catch rulings that both appeared to be wrong on the field, and not corrected by replay.

On Sunday afternoon, Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington caught a pass and had control with both feet down in the end zone, but it was ruled incomplete. On Sunday night, 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans didn't have full control with both feet down as he went out of bounds in the end zone, but it was ruled a touchdown.

In the Jaguars game, former NFL referee Gene Steratore broke the play down and explained that while there was some minor movement of the football as Washington went to the ground, Washington had the ball with both feet down and never lost control.

"When Parker Washington, after the bobble, possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he's falling," Steratore said on the CBS broadcast. "Then I had the left foot touch. I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football. I have possession, right foot down, tap with the left foot, yes, the ball moves a little, but the right hand, in my opinion, continues to keep that secure enough, that I would say in my opinion he's still controlling that football. I think it's a touchdown."

In the 49ers game, former NFL referee Terry McAulay said Evans was juggling the ball while running across the end zone and didn't have control of it until his final step, with only one foot down in bounds.

"I don't see him get final control until he's got one foot down," McAulay said. "The ball rolls around on his wrist. I don't see it pinned to his body. When he gets control, there's only one foot down. I think they should've reviewed it and reversed it to incomplete."

Even if the NFL wants to insist that its officials got both calls right on the field, and that the replay review process was correct to uphold those calls, the league still needs to acknowledge that it has a problem on its hands if the catch rule is so confusing that even former referees who now work as on-air officiating analysts aren't seeing what the on-field officials and the replay officials are seeing.

item.title: Jesse Minter: The only thing you can do is get up off the mat again
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: It has been a rough stretch for first-year head coach Jesse Minter and the Ravens, who have now lost six games in a row after falling to the Panthers on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
It has been a rough stretch for first-year head coach Jesse Minter and the Ravens, who have now lost six games in a row after falling to the Panthers on Sunday.

After a back-and-forth game that ended up in a loss, Minter said that every loss is tough.

“The last two weeks, our team has battled their butts off and put the team in position to have a chance to win. We haven’t gotten it done,” Minter said, via transcript from the team. “And so again, you’re going to look back. We’re going to come in tomorrow. We’re going to look at all these different plays and say, '[It] could’ve been this play, or it could’ve been that play. Can’t do that.' It’s a one-play-at-a-time game, and we didn’t get it done.”

“The only thing you can do is get up off the mat again,” Minter added. “[It was] two really tough, gut-wrenching type of games, but again, it’s an opportunity. Every day’s an opportunity to bounce back. Every day is an opportunity to improve. We’ll go right back to work.”

Now a few games behind in the AFC North, the Ravens will be on the road again to face the Texans in Week 12 before a Week 13 bye.

item.title: Panthers come back to beat Ravens in a wild game in Carolina
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In a crazy, back-and-forth game, the Panthers ended up on top, 35-33.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers and Ravens played a highly entertaining game today at Carolina, going back and forth until the closing seconds, when an ill-advised Jacoby Brissett interception ended the Ravens' hopes.

Brissett played well for most of the game, but when he attempted to make a play in the final 30 seconds, he scrambled around before heaving the ball deep downfield, where it was intercepted by the Panthers, sealing a 35-33 win.

Other than that interception, Brissett was solid, completing 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown. Derrick Henry and Justice Hill both had rushing touchdowns for the Ravens, but Henry went into the locker room late in the game for a concussion evaluation.

Panthers quarterback Bryce Young shook off some early struggles and finished 22 of 30 for 254 yards, with two touchdowns and an interception. Chuba Hubbard had an excellent game for the Panthers, running 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns.

With the win, the Panthers improve to 5-5 and remain atop the NFC South. The Ravens fall to 4-7.

item.title: DK Metcalf should have been ejected earlier than he was, for contact with official
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's another factor that could fuel a Metcalf suspension.
item.content:encoded:
As it turns out, Steelers receiver DK Metcalf should have been ejected before he was ejected.

It happened in connection with the first of two personal fouls that prompted his disqualification. After being separated from Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean following a play that began with 12:52 to play in the third quarter, umpire Mark Pellis pushed Metcalf away from the fray. Pellis had his hand on Metcalf's chest.

Metcalf can be seen slapping Pellis's forearm away.

From Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1(e): "Under no circumstance is a player allowed to shove, push, or strike an official in an offensive, disrespectful, or unsportsmanlike manner. The player shall be disqualified from the game, and any such action must be reported to the Commissioner, who may impose further discipline."

Metcalf should have been disqualified then and there, because "shall" means "must."

It wasn't part of a broader fray, with Metcalf not knowing whose arm he was striking. It was Metcalf and Pellis, and no one else.

Later in the quarter, Metcalf drew a second personal foul and was ejected. As the league considers the next step for potential discipline of Metcalf, his contact with Pellis should be a factor in determining whether to suspend Metcalf for Friday's game against the Broncos — if not longer.
